problems.title: Depth-loss inputs are warped RGB tensors
problems.source_location: Section 3.1, PDF p.5, Eqs.(8)–(9); Warp/newCodes/train.py, lines 78–115
claim: Section 3.1, Eqs.(8)–(9), defines an alignment loss on the estimated depth maps. The released transformation trainer instead passes the RGB warp outputs into that discrepancy.
analysis: Equal depth maps under identity geometry should give identical compared depth tensors and zero residual. The traced RGB arguments can differ despite those equal depths; the finite identity-geometry example yields \(7/3\) rather than \(0\). This follows from the input dataflow and does not require a trained model.
result: The released loss call mixes modalities. It does not identify which historical training program produced the paper’s tables.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Warp the depth maps and validity masks with the already predicted transformations, then compare those depth outputs. For equal nonconstant maps under identity geometry, each residual vanishes directly.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a local training implementation mismatch without a quantified effect on the core paper results.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Deployment conversion freezes replacement decoder modules during training
problems.source_location: Section 3.2, PDF pp.5–6, Eq.(14); Fusion/newCodes/network.py, build_model and RepConvN.fuse_convs; Fusion/newCodes/train.py, lines 42–48, 77 and 105
claim: Section 3.2 describes optimizing the fusion-mask network. `Fusion/newCodes/train.py` constructs its optimizer before `build_model` invokes deployment conversion inside the training loop.
analysis: The conversion replaces branch parameters with frozen convolution modules. The optimizer retains the old parameter objects, while the replacements are not trainable. Backpropagation therefore cannot perform the intended decoder-branch updates. This concerns the decoder path, rather than a blanket prohibition on branch fusion in the separate transformation estimator.
result: The public fusion trainer does not preserve the intended trainable decoder parameterization. The historical experimental path remains unidentified.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use the unconverted decoder during training and convert an evaluation copy after optimization. Training a fused architecture is a different recipe and requires trainable replacement parameters and a matching optimizer.
problems.impact_rationale: The release defect is established, but no central experimental result is remeasured or shown invalid.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.

problems.title: Constant depth maps make min–max normalization undefined
claim: `Warp/newCodes/loss.py`, lines 134–165, normalizes with pooled minimum \(m\), maximum \(M\), and denominator \(M-m\).
analysis: For equal constant maps, \(M=m\), so both normalized maps contain \(0/0\). This boundary is finite and nonempty; it is the normalizer, rather than the underlying geometric comparison, that is undefined.
result: The public loss requires a constant-map convention. The frequency of this boundary in the reported training data is unknown.
assumptions: Only the cited paper version and explicitly described mathematical or implementation conditions are assessed.
repair: Use a documented positive floor \(s=\max(M-m,\epsilon)\), \(\epsilon>0\), or explicitly map equal constant inputs to zero residual. The floor must suit the representation and precision.
problems.impact_rationale: This is a bounded numerical-domain defect, not evidence of central method failure.
problems.existing_correction_status: An explicit local correction is described; author adoption and a corresponding published erratum are not established.
